sponsor: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and 67 original cosponsors
status: Introduced February 7, 2019. Referred to eleven committees. Not voted on in the House

cls.banner: This states an opinion of the House of Representatives. Even if adopted, it would not change the law, direct any agency or spend any money, and it would not go to the Senate or the President.
cls.checks: Loophole, enforcement and funding checks are switched off, because there is nothing to enforce. The analysis compares stated goals to legal effect and shows what a binding version would have to contain.

stated.t: Recognizing the duty of the Federal Government to create a Green New Deal.

A new national, social, industrial, and economic mobilization on a scale not seen since World War II and the New Deal era is a historic opportunity to create millions of good, high-wage jobs, provide unprecedented levels of prosperity and economic security, and counteract systemic injustices.

marketed.t: The nonbinding resolution seeks to eliminate U.S. greenhouse gas emissions within a decade and transition the economy away from fossil fuels.
A release on the 2023 Senate reintroduction says the resolution "directs Congress to act urgently to protect the planet".
The resolution is "not a law but a nonbinding symbol of congressional sentiment".

ladder.mechanism: Put the House on record that the federal government has a duty to create a Green New Deal.
ladder.outcome: A shared framework of goals that later bills can be measured against.
ladder.aim: Net-zero emissions, millions of jobs and greater economic security through a ten-year national mobilization.

promises.p: Recognize a federal duty to create a Green New Deal
promises.why: Adoption would record the House's opinion that the duty exists. A simple resolution cannot create a legal duty.
Stated as a goal. No provision caps, prices or regulates emissions, and the resolved clause gives no date for net-zero.

promises.p: Eliminate U.S. emissions within a decade
promises.why: The text says the goals "should be accomplished through a 10-year national mobilization". It does not say when the ten years begin or that net-zero must be reached by their end.
A sense-of resolution expresses an opinion. It cannot direct Congress, a committee or an agency to do anything.

promises.p: Millions of good, high-wage jobs and a job guarantee
promises.why: No program, agency, eligibility rule or funding is created.

promises.p: 100 percent clean, renewable and zero-emission power
promises.why: A goal with no standard, deadline or definition of which sources qualify.

questions.q: What would be legally different the day after the House adopted this?
questions.a: Nothing. A simple resolution speaks for one chamber, is not sent to the Senate or the President, and has no force of law. The Congressional Research Service notes that agencies may still watch such measures as a signal of what Congress might do later.

questions.q: For each goal, which words would deliver it?
questions.a: None of the goals is paired with an operative provision. The verbs are "it is the duty", "should be accomplished" and "will require". There is no "shall", no agency, no appropriation and no amendment to any statute.

questions.q: Even as a statement of goals, where does the wording leave room?
questions.a: Four emissions goals are qualified by "as much as technologically feasible". Net-zero has no date in the resolved clause. "Clean, renewable, and zero-emission" energy is not defined, so the text does not settle whether nuclear power or fossil generation with carbon capture counts.

questions.q: Who is assigned to do anything?
questions.a: "The Federal Government" as a whole. No department, agency, official or committee is named.

questions.q: What would this cost, and where is the money?
questions.a: The resolution contains no cost figure and provides no funding. Because it has no budgetary effect, no official cost estimate would be prepared for it.

questions.q: Has this text ever been voted on?
questions.a: Not in the House. The Senate majority leader introduced the same text as a joint resolution, and on March 26, 2019 a motion to take it up failed with 0 votes in favor, 57 against and 43 senators voting present.

questions.q: Do binding bills exist that carry parts of this framework?
questions.a: Yes. Sponsors have introduced separate bills, including a Green New Deal for Public Housing Act and Civilian Climate Corps legislation, and a bill to establish a Green New Deal for public schools was introduced in July 2026. Those are the vehicles where loophole analysis applies.

s.l: Reintroduction of the Green New Deal for Public Housing Act

questions.q: What would a binding version of the first goal need?
questions.a: A statutory emissions target with dates, a named agency with authority to set and enforce limits, a funding source, and a way to enforce the target against the government itself. The "binding version" table in the bigger picture panel sets this out goal by goal.

a.q: it is the sense of the House of Representatives

findings.title: The resolution expresses the sense of the House and would have no force of law if adopted.
findings.plain: The words "it is the sense of the House" mean the House is stating a view. Nothing after those words can require anyone to do anything, whatever the language says.
findings.tech: A simple resolution (H. Res.) is adopted by one chamber and is not presented to the President. The Congressional Research Service describes sense-of measures as not legally binding. Every paragraph that follows depends grammatically on this clause.
findings.use: A member can cite a vote or cosponsorship as action on climate without any change in law.

inq.q: What actually happened to this text in Congress, and what does that show about its function?

items.h: Introduced three times, never voted on in the House
items.d: H. Res. 109 in 2019 with 101 cosponsors, H. Res. 332 in 2021 with 104, and H. Res. 319 in 2023 with 96. Each was referred to committee and went no further.

items.h: The one vote was arranged by opponents
items.d: The Senate majority leader introduced the same text as S.J. Res. 8. The motion to take it up failed 0 to 57 with 43 voting present.

The Congressional Research Service describes sense-of measures as not legally binding because they are never presented to the President, while noting that agencies may watch them as a signal of what Congress might do.

inq.open: Cosponsor counts come from a secondary table and should be confirmed against Congress.gov.

two.dec: Will binding legislation be introduced to implement the resolution's goals?

views.why: Treat the resolution as an organizing framework and a commitment to return to.
A non-binding text can be brought up for a vote to put members on record.
Note only that it does not bind anyone.

a.q: it is the duty of the Federal Government to create a Green New Deal

findings.title: The resolution declares a federal duty and assigns it to no agency or official.
findings.plain: The resolution says the federal government has a duty. It does not name a department, an official or a deadline, so no one in particular would be responsible.
findings.tech: Binding mandates name an officer ("the Administrator shall"). "The Federal Government" is not an entity that can be ordered, sued or funded as such.

a.q: should be accomplished through a 10-year national mobilization

findings.title: The ten-year mobilization is framed with "should" and has no stated start date.
findings.plain: The goals "should be accomplished" through a ten-year mobilization. "Should" is a recommendation, and the text does not say when the ten years begin.
findings.tech: "Should" is hortatory in drafting practice. The phrase "10-year national mobilization" has no start date, and the 2021 and 2023 reintroductions carried the same ten-year language forward.
findings.use: The timeline can be described as beginning whenever a speaker chooses.

a.q: as much as is technologically feasible

findings.title: Four emissions goals are qualified by "as much as is technologically feasible", with no designated decision-maker.
findings.plain: For infrastructure, manufacturing, agriculture and transportation, the goal is to remove emissions "as much as technologically feasible". The text does not say who decides what is feasible.
findings.tech: In a binding statute this qualifier hands the standard to whoever judges feasibility, usually the regulated industry's own evidence. It appears here four times, in subparagraphs (B)(i), (F), (G) and (H) of paragraph (2).
findings.use: If carried into a binding bill unchanged, each sector's goal would be only as strong as the feasibility finding.

findings.title: The net-zero goal has no date, baseline or accounting method in the resolving clause.
findings.plain: The first goal is net-zero greenhouse gas emissions. The resolution does not say by when, measured how, or what counts as an offset.
findings.tech: The preamble cites a need for net-zero global emissions by 2050. The resolved clause links the goals to a ten-year mobilization but sets no net-zero date. "Net" implies removals or offsets, which are not defined.
findings.use: Supporters and critics can each describe the target differently, and both can point to the text.

s.l: Coverage describing the goal as elimination within a decade

two.dec: Would binding legislation set a date for net-zero emissions?

views.why: Describe the target as elimination within a decade.

a.q: clean, renewable, and zero-emission energy sources

findings.title: The resolution does not specify which energy sources qualify as "clean, renewable, and zero-emission".
findings.plain: All power is to come from "clean, renewable, and zero-emission" sources. The text does not say whether a source must be all three or any one, which decides whether nuclear power counts.
findings.tech: Nuclear generation is zero-emission but not renewable. Fossil generation with carbon capture is arguably neither. Leaving the list open can be a way to hold a coalition together, which is why this is marked as a trade-off.
findings.use: The ambiguity moves the decision to whatever binding bill comes later.

a.q: guaranteeing a job with a family-sustaining wage

findings.title: The resolution refers to guaranteeing employment and establishes no program, eligibility rule or funding.
findings.plain: The resolution speaks of "guaranteeing a job" to everyone in the United States. A guarantee needs a program, an employer of last resort, rules and money. None is here.
findings.tech: The same is true of "guaranteeing universal access to clean water" and "providing all people of the United States with high-quality health care". In a non-binding text these are statements of aim.
findings.use: The word "guaranteeing" can be quoted as if a guarantee had been enacted.

findings.pat: One chamber cannot bind future legislation

a.q: ensuring that any infrastructure bill considered by Congress addresses climate change

findings.title: The resolution calls for conditions on future infrastructure legislation that a simple resolution cannot impose.
findings.plain: The resolution calls for ensuring that any infrastructure bill Congress considers addresses climate change. A statement of opinion by one chamber cannot control what later bills contain.
findings.tech: A chamber can bind its own proceedings through its rules, for example with a point of order. A sense-of resolution is not a rule.

findings.title: The quantitative targets appear in the preamble, which has no operative effect.
findings.plain: The specific numbers, such as the 1.5 degree limit and the 2050 date, are in the "Whereas" clauses. Those explain why the House is speaking. They are not part of what it resolves.
findings.tech: Preambles and findings can inform interpretation but create no rights or duties. Here the most concrete targets in the document sit outside the resolved clause.
findings.use: Preamble figures are often quoted as if they were commitments.

findings.title: The resolution contains no cost estimate and no authorization or appropriation of funds.
findings.plain: The resolution names goals that would require very large public investment. It contains no cost figure and provides no funding, and a resolution could not provide any.
findings.tech: Only a bill or joint resolution that becomes law can authorize or appropriate funds. Paragraph (4)(A) refers to "adequate capital" through grants, public banks and public financing without amounts.
findings.use: Cost estimates from supporters and opponents cannot be checked against the text, because the text has none.

findings.pat: Vote taken on a different vehicle
findings.title: The House did not vote on the resolution, and the Senate vote on a companion text failed 0 to 57.
findings.plain: The House never voted on this resolution. The Senate held a procedural vote on a copy introduced by the majority leader. It failed 0 to 57, with 43 senators voting present.
findings.tech: S.J. Res. 8 carried the same text as a joint resolution. Supporters of the House resolution called the vote a tactic and voted present. The episode shows how a non-binding text can be used to put members on record.
findings.use: Either side can cite the vote: as proof of no support, or as proof of a sham process.

findings.title: Separate bills introduced under the Green New Deal name would carry binding provisions.
findings.plain: People looking for what would change the law should look at the separate bills introduced under the Green New Deal name, such as those on public housing and a climate jobs corps.
findings.tech: Those are bills (H.R. and S.), which would be binding if enacted and can be red-teamed for loopholes in the ordinary way.

s.l: Green New Deal for Public Housing Act reintroduction

bigger.lead: The resolution names nearly every part of the climate and economic agenda. Because it has no legal effect, it reaches none of them. The table shows what it names; the second table shows what a binding measure would need for each goal.

map.note: Net-zero stated as a goal; no cap, price or standard.
100 percent clean, renewable and zero-emission; sources undefined.

map.part: Health care, housing and economic security
map.note: Listed as things a Green New Deal will require.
Later spending and tax law on clean energy was enacted through separate bills, which sponsors of the 2023 reintroduction cited.

s.l: Sen. Wyden release on the 2023 reintroduction

binding.need: A statutory target with dates and interim milestones; an agency with authority to set and enforce limits; a rule for what counts as an offset; a consequence if a milestone is missed.
A definition of qualifying sources; a standard that applies to utilities; a compliance schedule; penalties or alternative compliance payments.
A program and administering agency; eligibility and wage rules; an appropriation or mandatory funding stream.
Authorized programs with appropriations; standards; a delivery mechanism through States, localities or direct federal work.
Enforceable criteria for which communities qualify; a required share of investment; reporting and a right to challenge allocations.

others.n: Another binding companion, currently in committee.

others.n: Reintroduced with similar text; neither was voted on.

stake.want: A shared framework and a public commitment to build on. Movement groups endorsed the resolution.
Job and wage guarantees, and protection for workers in industries that would shrink. Some unions endorsed it.

stake.role: Fossil fuel companies and their workers
stake.want: No binding phase-out, or the longest possible timeline.
Clear rules on which power sources will count, and time to build.
Explicit inclusion of nuclear power as clean energy.
A cost figure and a funding source before any commitment.

stake.role: Communities named in the text as frontline and vulnerable
stake.want: Enforceable priority in investment, not only a mention.
A statement of direction that later bills can carry out.
A recorded vote that puts supporters on record. The Senate vote was arranged by the measure's opponents.
Describe sense-of measures as having no force of law.

stake.role: A judge who reads statutes by their text
stake.want: Applies the words as written and will not supply what Congress left out.

stake.role: A judge who reads statutes by their purpose
stake.want: Resolves doubt in favor of what the law was trying to do.
Wants every key term defined, every reference checked and every relationship to existing law stated.

conf_note: The Green New Deal resolution assigns no duties to any agency or official, so there is no responsible party whose independence can be assessed. A later law that carried out its goals would need this review.
